parameters.name: RPL subject to IURC jurisdiction
parameters.doc_value: all residential and non-residential customers receiving electric distribution service from RPL
parameters.s1_quote: these rules shall apply to any electrical public utility subject to the jurisdiction of the commission

parameters.name: Customer dispute access channels
parameters.doc_value: telephone, web form, email, written letter, in person at any RPL service center, executive office referral, or IURC Consumer Affairs portal referral
parameters.s1_quote: by telephone. (2) in writing. (3) through the utility's website. (4) at the utility's business office. (5) by any other method made available by the utility.

parameters.name: Required dispute record fields
parameters.doc_value: customer name; service address; customer contact telephone number, if available; customer account number; general nature of the dispute
parameters.s1_quote: (1) the customer's name. (2) the customer's service address. (3) the telephone number at which the customer may be contacted, if such number is available. (4) the customer's account number. (5) the general nature of the dispute.

parameters.name: Post-decision no-disconnect window
parameters.doc_value: sooner than 10 days after a decision by consumer affairs or the commission
parameters.s1_quote: sooner than ten (10) days after a decision by consumer affairs or the commission.

parameters.name: Service continuation condition
parameters.doc_value: while the utility's proposed resolution is under review by consumer affairs or the commission
parameters.s1_quote: while the utility's proposed resolution is under review by consumer affairs or the commission

parameters.name: Bill delinquency period
parameters.doc_value: 17 days after the initial bill is postmarked
parameters.s1_quote: a bill is considered delinquent unless payment is received within seventeen (17) days after the initial bill is postmarked.

parameters.name: Undisputed amount formula — fraction of annual billing
parameters.doc_value: one-twelfth (1/12) of the estimated annual billing
parameters.s1_quote: an amount equal to one-twelfth (1/12) of the estimated annual billing for service to be rendered to the customer.

parameters.name: Minimum tenure for using actual average
parameters.doc_value: at least 12 months
parameters.s1_quote: for a customer who has been a customer for at least twelve (12) months, the estimate will be based on the customer's average bill for the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the disputed bill.

parameters.name: 17-day nonpenalty period
parameters.doc_value: 17-day nonpenalty period
parameters.s1_quote: printed statements or actual figures, or both, on either side of the bill must inform the customer of the seventeen (17) day nonpenalty period.

parameters.name: Disconnection hours — earliest
parameters.s1_quote: no utility may disconnect service unless it is done between the hours of 8:00 a.m. and 3:00 p.m., prevailing local time.

parameters.name: Disconnection hours — latest
parameters.s1_quote: no utility may disconnect service unless it is done between the hours of 8:00 a.m. and 3:00 p.m., prevailing local time.

parameters.name: Residential disconnect notice period
parameters.doc_value: 14 days prior written notice
parameters.s1_quote: electric service to any residential customer shall not be disconnected for a violation of any rule or regulation of a utility or for the nonpayment of a bill, except after fourteen (14) days prior written notice to the customer

parameters.name: Customer appeal window to consumer affairs
parameters.doc_value: within 7 days of the date the proposed resolution is received
parameters.s1_quote: a complaint must be submitted under this section within seven (7) days of the date the customer receives the utility's proposed resolution.

parameters.name: Day-of-act exclusion in time period computation
parameters.doc_value: the day on which the customer receives the determination is not counted
parameters.s1_quote: the day of the act from which the designated period of time begins to run shall not be included.

parameters.name: Additional info response to consumer affairs
parameters.doc_value: within 14 days unless consumer affairs directs otherwise
parameters.s1_quote: to which parties must respond within fourteen (14) days unless otherwise directed by consumer affairs.

parameters.name: Consumer affairs decision deadline
parameters.doc_value: within 30 days of the complaint submission date
parameters.s1_quote: provide a decision to the customer and the utility within thirty (30) days of the complaint submission date

parameters.name: Director review request window
parameters.doc_value: within 7 days of the date of receipt of the proposed resolution
parameters.s1_quote: either party may request a review by the director of consumer affairs or director's designee within seven (7) days of the date of receipt of the proposed resolution of the informal complaint.

parameters.name: Commission review request window
parameters.doc_value: within 20 days of the date of receipt of the director's decision
parameters.s1_quote: either party may request commission review of the consumer affairs' decision under ic 8-1-2-34.5 within twenty (20) days of the date of receipt of the decision of the director of consumer affairs' or director's designee.

parameters.name: Commission copies to opposing party and OUCC
parameters.doc_value: within 7 days from the date the review is requested
parameters.s1_quote: upon receiving a request for commission review, the commission shall provide a copy of the request to the opposing party and the office of the utility consumer counselor (oucc) within seven (7) days from the date the review is requested.

parameters.name: Customer informal complaint filing window
parameters.doc_value: within 7 days of the date the customer receives RPL's proposed resolution
parameters.s1_quote: a complaint must be submitted under this section within seven (7) days of the date the customer receives the utility's proposed resolution.

parameters.name: Hardship payment — maximum initial payment
parameters.doc_value: lesser of $10 or one-tenth (1/10) of the bill
parameters.s1_quote: pays a reasonable portion (not to exceed ten dollars ($10) or one-tenth (1/10) of the bill, whichever is less, unless the customer agrees to a greater portion) of the bill

parameters.name: Hardship arrangement — remainder payment window
parameters.doc_value: within 3 months
parameters.s1_quote: agrees to pay the remainder of the outstanding bill within three (3) months

parameters.name: Prior breach lookback period
parameters.doc_value: within the past 12 months
parameters.s1_quote: has not breached any similar agreement with the utility made pursuant to this section within the past twelve (12) months

parameters.name: Utility-error bill — maximum initial payment
parameters.doc_value: reasonable portion not exceeding an amount equal to the customer's average bill for the 6 bills immediately preceding the bill in question
parameters.qualifier: not to exceed average of preceding
parameters.s1_quote: pays a reasonable portion of the bill, not to exceed an amount equal to the customer's average bill for the six (6) bills immediately preceding the bill in question

parameters.name: No late fee on utility-error arrangement
parameters.doc_value: RPL may not add a late fee to this arrangement
parameters.s1_quote: the utility may not add to the outstanding bill any late fee

parameters.name: Annual IURC complaint report contents
parameters.doc_value: number of complaints received, general nature of subject matter, how each complaint was received, whether a commission review was conducted
parameters.s1_quote: each utility shall annually submit a report to the commission that shall state and classify the number of complaints made to the utility under section 3 of this rule, the general nature of the subject matter thereof, how the complaint was received, and whether a commission review was conducted thereon.

parameters.name: Records retention minimum
parameters.doc_value: 6 months from the date of final resolution
parameters.s1_quote: the utility shall retain records of disputes received under this rule and the resolutions thereof for a period of six (6) months from the date of final resolution of the dispute under this rule

parameters.name: Appeal window stated on CS-F-032
parameters.doc_value: within 7 days of the date you receive this letter
parameters.s1_quote: a complaint must be submitted under this section within seven (7) days of the date the customer receives the utility's proposed resolution.

parameters.name: Filing deadline on App-D
parameters.doc_value: within 7 days of the date you receive Rockridge Power's written determination
parameters.s1_quote: a complaint must be submitted under this section within seven (7) days of the date the customer receives the utility's proposed resolution.

parameters.name: CA decision period stated on App-D
parameters.doc_value: within 30 days of your complaint submission date
parameters.s1_quote: provide a decision to the customer and the utility within thirty (30) days of the complaint submission date

parameters.name: Director review and commission review on App-D
parameters.doc_value: within 7 days of receiving that decision; within 20 days of the Director's decision
parameters.s1_quote: either party may request a review by the director of consumer affairs or director's designee within seven (7) days of the date of receipt of the proposed resolution of the informal complaint.

interpretations.question: What language access methods are required beyond English and Spanish?
interpretations.position: Company position: RPL uses a third-party telephonic interpreter service for languages other than English or Spanish, targeting connection within 5 minutes of request. This is company practice; the pack requires no specific method or timeframe.
interpretations.rationale: 170 IAC 16-1-4(a) requires channels for customers to bring disputes to the utility's attention but does not specify language access methods. RPL adopts the broader approach to serve its diverse service territory.

interpretations.question: Are CIS hold codes a regulatory concept or company practice?
interpretations.position: Company position: CIS hold codes HDSP and HIURC are RPL's internal system implementation of the service protection requirements in 170 IAC 16-1-7 and 170 IAC 16-1-4. The codes themselves are company practice; the protection obligations are regulatory.
interpretations.rationale: The pack requires service continuation and notification to stop collection activity during disputes but does not specify a system code mechanism.
